ambiguities.evidence: Display (2.21) on printed page 33 explicitly defines ||X||_{psi_1} as inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.
ambiguities.impact: The prose cross-reference is inconsistent, but display (2.21) and the proof of Lemma 2.7.6 unambiguously fix the norm formula used in this contract.
ambiguities.issue: Definition 2.7.5 says 'smallest K3 in property 3' although Proposition 2.7.1 labels its properties a--d and the bounded-at-one-point parameter there is K4.

contract_plain_english: A real random variable X is sub-gaussian exactly when its square is sub-exponential. In that case the psi_1 norm of X squared is exactly the square of the psi_2 norm of X. There are no centering or independence assumptions.

source_evidence.observation: The source states that X is sub-gaussian if and only if X^2 is sub-exponential, and exactly ||X^2||_{psi_1} = ||X||_{psi_2}^2.
The proof identifies the infimum condition E exp(X^2/K) <= 2 for ||X^2||_{psi_1} with E exp(X^2/L^2) <= 2 for ||X||_{psi_2} under K = L^2.
The source defines sub-gaussianity through Proposition 2.5.2 and defines ||X||_{psi_2} as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.
The source defines sub-exponentiality through Proposition 2.7.1 and defines ||Z||_{psi_1} as inf {t > 0 : E exp(|Z|/t) <= 2}.

conclusions: X is sub-gaussian if and only if X^2 is sub-exponential.
definitions_and_conventions: X^2 denotes the pointwise square of X; hence |X^2| = X^2.
Sub-gaussian and sub-exponential mean the respective equivalent-property classes of Definitions 2.5.6 and 2.7.5.
implicit_context: Expectation is taken on the underlying probability space of X.
No centering or independence premise is imposed.

details: Both directions are asserted: sub-gaussianity of X implies sub-exponentiality of X^2, and sub-exponentiality of X^2 implies sub-gaussianity of X.
The psi_1 norm of the square equals the square of the psi_2 norm, with exact constant 1.
The proof uses K = L^2 to identify the two defining exponential-moment conditions.

undebatable_constraints: The class relationship is an if-and-only-if statement, not merely one implication.
The transformed variable is exactly X^2.
The norm conclusion is the exact equality ||X^2||_{psi_1} = ||X||_{psi_2}^2, not an inequality up to an absolute constant.
No mean-zero, symmetry, or independence assumption appears.
The psi_2 definition from PDF page 16 / printed page 27 is required context for the equality.
